source.title: Characterizing Learning in Deep Neural Networks using Tractable Algorithmic Complexity Analysis
source.authors: Pedram Bakhtiarifard; Sophia N. Wilson; Mahmoud Afifi; Jonathan Wenshoj; Raghavendra Selvan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on a modular-addition task, but adds QuBD complexity measurement rather than reproducing the original study's measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports one modular-addition grokking experiment. Its Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 results concern learning, generalization, and overfitting, but do not report grokking-like delayed generalization on those datasets. Other cited grokking findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper re-runs the Power et al. modular-addition grokking setup (P = 97, 50% split) with a 2-layer MLP instead of a transformer. It reports delayed validation improvement long after training error reaches zero, which bears directly on V1. Its main contribution, the QuBD weight-complexity measure, is a different construct from V2's generalizing circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors say QuBD complexity 'follows' grokking: it stays high while validation loss is high, then decreases once validation loss has reached zero (not 'as' it reaches zero). It continues decreasing afterward, which they read as further algorithmic simplification, in contrast to overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modular-addition task described as following Power et al. (2021), with a 2-layered MLP [512, 256], P = 97, a 50%/50% split of the full Cartesian product, and QuBD complexity measurement. The text does not give enough detail to compare the full training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: QuBD weight-complexity reduction stays high during the high-validation-loss phase. It drops once validation loss reaches zero and keeps dropping afterward; this contrasts with the rise in complexity during overfitting on Fashion-MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Algorithmic (KCS) complexity of network weights falls at and after the grokking transition rather than before it, so this weight-complexity measure does not anticipate the jump.

record.problems: The grokking evidence is from one reported modular-addition setup. The paper does not report test accuracy or chance-level accuracy, does not test delay against training-set size, and gives no uncertainty estimate for the grokking result.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly test delayed generalization in the claim's settings. The Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 learning-curve results do not report grokking-like delays; cited findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only a 50% split is run); chance-level test accuracy before the jump (only loss is reported); repeat seeds for the grokking run.
Whole version: no circuit identification, no Fourier analysis, no memorization-removal measure, and no mechanistic progress measure.
Whole version: the Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 runs show ordinary learning and overfitting, not a grokking-like delay; no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Whole version: no weight-decay variation, critical dataset size or ungrokking.

record.verdict_notes: The grokking evidence is a single, briefly described experiment (about 5 minutes of compute). Optimizer and weight decay for the grokking run are not stated explicitly; Appx. E.4 says only that it follows a 'similar setup', which elsewhere uses Adam with weight decay 0.01. No seeds or uncertainty are given for this run. The original sources are Power et al. and Nanda et al.; this paper is neither.

versions.untested_parts: The training-set-size dependence of the delay is not tested. The paper reports error and loss, not train/test accuracy trajectories or chance-level accuracy.
It does not identify a generalizing circuit, measure Fourier structure or removal of memorizing components, or show that the complexity measure anticipates the transition.
No grokking-like delay is tested on non-algorithmic data or through initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test whether low-norm bias or weight decay selects an efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs.
It does not test optimizer or numerical-artifact explanations.
